items.title: US jury convicts pastor over 2021 killing of Haiti's president
items.why: A federal jury in Miami found Haitian-American pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon guilty on Wednesday on all eight charges over the plot to kill Haiti's President Jovenel Moïse, shot dead at home in July 2021. He faces up to life in prison; sentencing is on 10 February.
items.matters: His lawyer says he will appeal. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people over the killing.

items.title: UN's top court rules on Thursday on Myanmar Rohingya genocide case
items.why: The International Court of Justice in The Hague is due to say from 09:00 GMT on Thursday whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. The Gambia brought the case in 2019 after a 2017 army offensive drove at least 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. Myanmar denies genocide.
items.matters: The ruling is final and cannot be appealed; about 1.2 million Rohingya live in refugee camps in Bangladesh.

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m at New York auction
items.why: Vincent van Gogh's "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", painted in 1890, the year he died, sold at Sotheby's in New York on Wednesday for $190.4m including fees. The previous auction record for his work was $117.2m, set in 2022.
items.matters: The sale followed a last-minute settlement with heirs of a German former owner, who say his family sold it under Nazi-era pressure.

items.title: Bancroft says whole Australian team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plot
items.why: Former Australia batter Cameron Bancroft wrote in The West Australian on Wednesday that "the whole team" knew sandpaper was being used on the ball in South Africa in 2018, not only the three players punished. Captain Pat Cummins has called such claims "complete and utter nonsense".
items.matters: Cricket Australia says it will consider his account but will not reopen its investigation.

items.title: US Federal Reserve minutes point to an interest rate rise in December
items.why: Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, published on Wednesday, show nearly all policymakers think raising rates again would likely be appropriate to bring inflation back to 2%. The Fed held its key rate at 3.75% to 4% in October after raising it in September.
items.matters: Higher US rates make borrowing dearer around the world; markets see about a 95% chance of a December rise, AP reports.

items.title: US and Venezuela agree to restore military ties during Hegseth visit
items.why: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement on joint training and intelligence sharing during a surprise visit to Venezuela's capital, Caracas, on Wednesday. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez called it a resumption of military ties. She took over after US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January.
items.matters: Hegseth called Venezuela a "compliant security partner"; few details of the deal have been published.

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black US House speaker
items.why: House Democrats voted 251 to 11 on Wednesday to nominate Hakeem Jeffries of New York as speaker of the US House of Representatives. With Democrats taking control after the midterms, the full House is expected to elect him when it meets on 3 January.

items.title: Ghana's central bank cuts its main interest rate from 14% to 11%
items.why: The Bank of Ghana lowered its policy rate by three percentage points on Wednesday, to its lowest level in decades. Governor Johnson Pandit Asiama called it "a realignment, not a reduction", because market rates had already fallen below 14%. Inflation was 5.5% in October.
items.matters: Cheaper borrowing could ease costs for Ghanaian households and businesses; average bank lending rates have already fallen to about 16%.

items.title: Israel launches new military operation in central Gaza despite ceasefire
items.why: Israel's military began an operation in central Gaza on Wednesday against what it calls Hamas infrastructure, ordering residents of three blocks near the Bureij and Nuseirat camps to leave. Hamas calls it a flagrant ceasefire violation. Gaza's civil defence agency says Israeli strikes killed three people.
items.matters: Defence Minister Israel Katz says Israel will not withdraw until Hamas is dismantled.
items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: Israel told residents of three areas to leave.

items.title: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine, repayable only from Russian reparations
items.why: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed on Wednesday a €45bn loan to Ukraine for 2027: €20bn for its budget and €25bn for military needs. Ukraine would repay it only once Russia pays for war damage. EU member states must approve it.
items.matters: It would cover about two-thirds of Ukraine's expected €70bn funding gap next year; EU leaders discuss it at next week's summit.

items.title: Germany cuts electricity tax and plans fuel price cap from January
items.why: Germany's governing coalition agreed on Wednesday, after overnight talks, to cut electricity tax for households and small businesses from 2.05 cents to 0.1 cents per kWh for 2027. It also plans a three-month cap on petrol and diesel prices from 1 January.
items.matters: Energy prices rose after the Iran war disrupted Gulf shipping; the tax cut costs about €5bn a year.

items.title: Senegal's ruling party expels President Faye amid feud with Sonko
items.why: Pastef, which holds 130 of 165 seats in Senegal's parliament, said on Tuesday that President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 others had automatically lost their membership. Faye sacked party leader Ousmane Sonko as prime minister in May; Sonko is now parliament's speaker.
items.matters: The rift has stalled Senegal's budget and an IMF loan programme of about $2.2bn the country is waiting for.

items.title: US says string of tech outages is unrelated and not a cyberattack
items.why: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday there is "zero evidence" that recent outages are linked or caused by hackers or foreign actors. They include a worldwide Microsoft outage, a nationwide flight ground stop, problems at big US banks and a classified government network going offline.
items.matters: Microsoft and the US aviation regulator blamed technical faults during upgrades and found no sign of malicious activity.

items.title: Italy passes antisemitism law using the IHRA definition
items.why: Italy's lower house gave final approval on Tuesday night, by 147 votes to 93, to a law that adopts the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism. It creates no new crimes or penalties. Opponents say it could chill criticism of Israel; the government says such criticism remains protected.
items.matters: Italy's Antisemitism Observatory recorded 963 antisemitic incidents in 2025, almost four times the 2022 figure.

items.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% as diesel prices hit a record
items.why: Consumer prices in the UK rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday. Motor fuel was 33.2% dearer than a year earlier, with diesel averaging a record 199.5p a litre.
items.matters: Petrol and diesel drove the rise; the ONS says pump prices have eased in November as oil prices fell.

items.title: Arsenic in river from Myanmar mines cuts water to Thai villages
items.why: Thailand's prime minister has ordered officials to find new water sources for more than 20,000 households in Mae Sai, in northern Chiang Rai province. Arsenic in the Sai River has reached up to 28 times the safe limit; researchers link much of it to mining across the border in Myanmar.
items.matters: Officials fear the pollution is spreading into the Mekong, which millions of people in several countries rely on.

items.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat, the last midterm race decided
items.why: Mary Peltola beat Republican senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the AP and NBC News projected late on Tuesday, with about 50% of the vote. It was the last US Senate race of the midterms to be called; Democrats and their independent allies will hold 56 of 100 seats from January.
items.matters: Democrats flipped nine Senate seats this year, their biggest net gain since 1958, and will control the chamber.

items.title: Anthropic prices its share sale at $83, raising about $81bn
items.why: Anthropic, the US company behind the Claude AI models, sold 980 million shares at $83 each on Wednesday, above its planned $70 to $78 range, raising about $81bn. That values it at about $1.5 trillion; trading on Nasdaq starts on Thursday.
items.matters: Al Jazeera reports it is the largest stock market listing on record, ahead of SpaceX in June.
items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: shares were priced at $83, above the expected range.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI goes on sale on Thursday after long delays
items.why: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, priced at $79.99 in the US. It is the first new game in the series in 13 years.
items.matters: With a budget estimated at $1bn or more, it is one of the most expensive games ever made.

items.title: Pochettino ends US reign with win before joining Manchester United
items.why: The United States beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati on Tuesday, with goals from Christian Pulisic and 18-year-old Julian Hall, to reach the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals 8-0 on aggregate. It was Mauricio Pochettino's last game as US coach before he takes over at Manchester United.
items.matters: United are 18th in the Premier League; Pochettino's first match is against Liverpool on Sunday.

items.title: Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft one light-day from Earth
items.why: NASA's Voyager 1, launched in 1977, reached a distance of one light-day from Earth early on Wednesday: about 26 billion km, so far that its radio signals take a full day to reach us. A command and its reply now take two days.
items.matters: Its power is fading, and NASA's antennas are expected to lose its signal by about 2036.
items.changed: Updated 18 Nov: Voyager 1 has now passed the one light-day mark.

items.title: Fiji and Tonga declare drought emergencies as El Niño dries the Pacific
items.why: Fiji declared a nationwide state of disaster on Wednesday, with Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka saying the El Niño drought has reached crisis levels. The government has set aside FJ$20m for emergency water. Tonga has declared a 27-day state of emergency over water shortages.
items.matters: Fiji's weather service expects below-normal rain until April; experts say this El Niño could be among the strongest on record.

items.title: Gaza ceasefire body warns the truce could collapse without action
items.why: The US-backed Board of Peace told the UN Security Council on Tuesday that Israel and Hamas have fallen far short of their commitments under the 2025 ceasefire. It says Israel has not let Gaza's interim administration start work, and calls for more winter shelter supplies.
items.matters: The report says a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot last indefinitely.

items.title: Waymo pauses driverless freeway rides across the US after California ban
items.why: California's motor vehicles department has barred Waymo's driverless cars from the state's freeways, calling them an imminent hazard after vehicles drove into active construction zones. Waymo said on Tuesday it has also paused freeway rides in Phoenix, Austin and Miami; city-street rides continue.
items.matters: The ban lasts until Waymo shows it has fixed the problems; no end date has been given.

items.title: Haaland's late penalty sends Norway past Denmark into Nations League quarter-finals
items.why: Norway came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 in Copenhagen on Tuesday, with Erling Haaland scoring twice, including a penalty in the 96th minute. Norway finish second in their group behind Portugal; the quarter-final draw is on Friday 20 November.

items.title: Paraguay's attorney general resigns as lawmakers prepare to impeach him
items.why: Emiliano Rolón stepped down on Tuesday as opposition lawmakers moved to impeach him over his handling of investigations into the collapsed Ueno Bank and former president Santiago Peña. His office denies inaction or political interference.
items.matters: The bank's state takeover left hundreds of thousands of people locked out of their accounts, AFP reports.

items.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status
items.why: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) said on Tuesday that measles is again spreading continuously in the United States, Mexico and Bolivia, ending their elimination status. A day later, Pennsylvania reported its eighth measles death this year, an unvaccinated person; the state has 1,589 cases.
items.matters: PAHO says the setback can be reversed; the US must now send it a plan to stop the spread.
items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: Pennsylvania reported its eighth measles death of the year.

items.title: WHO says Congo's Ebola outbreak has more than doubled in three months
items.why: WHO head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Tuesday that more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths have been reported in eight provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 400 to 500 new cases a week. There is no approved vaccine for this Bundibugyo strain.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record; two candidate vaccines are due to join a trial within weeks.

items.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19
items.why: An Antonov An-12 transport plane crashed on Tuesday in an uninhabited area near Kemerovo, in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, Russia's defence ministry says. It gives a technical fault as the preliminary cause; an investigation is under way.

items.title: Quad leaders meet in Manila and plan first joint patrol-aircraft exercise
items.why: Donald Trump met the leaders of Australia, India and Japan in the Philippine capital, Manila, on Tuesday, his first Quad meeting since returning to office. They agreed a joint maritime patrol-aircraft exercise in 2027 and an AI accelerator for the Indo-Pacific.
items.matters: The four countries voiced concern about "economic coercion" without naming China, as tensions continue in the South China Sea.

items.title: Kosovo's former president Thaçi convicted of trying to obstruct justice
items.why: A Kosovo court sitting in The Hague found Hashim Thaçi guilty on Tuesday of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes case and sentenced him to 17 months. He is already serving 25 years, handed down in September, for war crimes in the 1998–99 war; he is appealing.
items.matters: Thaçi called the verdict "politics, not justice"; prosecutors had asked for six years.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China for first three-way summit
items.why: Donald Trump held separate talks with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, ahead of the three leaders' first three-way meeting at the APEC summit. Trump called Putin his "friend", saying "wonderful things can come out of this". It is their first meeting since August 2025.
items.matters: Ukraine, the Iran war, nuclear arms control, trade and AI are on the agenda; analysts expect few concrete agreements.
items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: Trump met Putin and Xi separately ahead of the three-way talks.

items.title: China cuts tariffs on Canadian pork and seafood after Xi–Carney talks
items.why: Meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday, President Xi Jinping and Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed to widen a January trade deal. China will cut tariffs on about C$400m (US$280m) of Canadian exports, including frozen pork and seafood; Canada extends exemptions for some Chinese steel and aluminium.
items.matters: Canada is deepening trade with China while its trade talks with the US remain unresolved.

items.title: Mongolia's president says he will resign over corruption allegations
items.why: President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa said on Tuesday he will step down after a former mayor of the capital, Ulaanbaatar, accused him of receiving $25m linked to a 2019 railway contract, AP reports. He denies wrongdoing and says he will cooperate with investigators.
items.matters: Parliament must accept the resignation; its speaker would then act as president, with an election due within four months.

items.changed: Updated 17 Nov: Ukraine says it brought down part of the road bridge to Crimea.
items.title: Ukraine collapses part of Crimea bridge after Russia hits Kyiv bridges
items.why: A road span of the Kerch Bridge, linking Russia to annexed Crimea, fell into the sea after Ukrainian missile and drone strikes overnight on Tuesday, Ukraine says; traffic is suspended. Russia says it will rebuild it. Russian strikes had hit two Kyiv bridges, cutting heating and water.
items.matters: The bridge is Russia's main supply route to Crimea. Crimea's Russian-installed governor says two people were killed in drone attacks there.

items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks for the third time in a week.
items.title: Iran targets US base in Kuwait after American strike on Qeshm Island
items.why: Iran's army says its drones targeted US air-defence systems at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base on Wednesday, after US jets hit a missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday. Kuwait and Bahrain say they intercepted the attacks. The US military says no US personnel were hurt.
items.matters: Qatar, a mediator, calls it a dangerous escalation; Trump, Xi and Putin are due to discuss the Iran war on Thursday.

items.title: Cyclone Akvan to hit India's Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coast on Friday
items.why: India's weather department (IMD) expects severe cyclonic storm Akvan to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by Friday afternoon, with winds of 90 to 100 km/h gusting to 110 km/h. Odisha's chief minister, Mohan Charan Majhi, says about 50,000 people have been evacuated.
items.matters: Odisha has issued red warnings for 13 districts and closed schools in six until Saturday; extremely heavy rain is forecast.
items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: the forecast landfall moved north towards Odisha; about 50,000 people evacuated.
Updated 18 Nov: the coalition launched new air strikes as the Houthis advance towards Aden.
items.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi sites as rebels push towards Aden
items.why: The Saudi-led coalition says it hit 60 Houthi military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada on Tuesday; the Houthis say at least 17 people were killed. Houthi forces are advancing towards Aden, the Yemeni government's base, and fighting continues around Taiz.
items.matters: The Houthis now hold the coast by the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route into the Red Sea.

items.changed: Updated 18 Nov: AFP reports deep divisions remain as the summit enters its final days.
items.title: COP31 talks deadlocked over fossil fuels and money as deadline nears
items.why: Ministers at the UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, remain split over a draft deal published on Monday that calls for faster action to move away from fossil fuels and for adaptation finance to triple to at least $120 billion a year by 2035.
items.matters: Talks are due to end on Friday 20 November; any deal needs the agreement of nearly 200 countries.
